To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) QTL for growth and feed efficiency in a broiler line were mapped to GGA2, 18 and 19, and QTL for growth in a layer line were mapped to 2, 3. 4 and 5.
the QTL for growth traits in the broiler x layer F(2) population were located in the same chromosomal regions as the QTL for the same traits found in the broiler F(2) and broiler F(3) populations.
1) QTL were detected in 3 out of the 4 traits analyzed, and 2) QTL were identified on GGA2 and GGA3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of growth and development in poultry and the use of molecular markers to detect and characterize quantitative trait loci.
the identification of chromosomal regions associated with performance traits.
identifying QTL that affect performance traits and the use of these QTL in marker-assisted selection (MAS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QTL for growth and intestinal length in chickens have been mapped in several chromosomal regions, and that QTL for these traits are likely to be pleiotropic and/or closely linked.
QTL mapping is a useful tool in the search for genes that control growth traits.
QTL were mapped on chromosomes 2, 3 4, 10, 18.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QTL for body weight and feed efficiency are located in the same regions of chromosomes 2 and 3.
GGA2, 4 and the distal region of GGA3 are important for chicken growth.

QTL for body weight and feed intake at 35 days are located on GGA2, 10, 18, 19 and 20, and QTL for body weights at 1, 41 and 42 days, and feed intake at days 35 to 42 are located on GGGs 1, 2, 3 4 and 5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QTL mapping using a broiler x line-cross is a viable approach to map QTL for performance traits.
the F2 broiler x layer population has the potential to be used as a resource population for QTL mapping.
the F2 population is an excellent tool for QTL mapping.
